parsed.target_users: people whose 3pm quick sync has run twenty minutes over every week since March

parsed.target_users: engineers who reconstruct yesterday from browser history thirty seconds before stand-up

parsed.name: Toaster Pro
parsed.description: Browns bread to order; R&D says "it's fine"

parsed.name: Crustodian
parsed.description: A palm-sized fridge robot that guards the last slice of pizza and reports, with photographic evidence, exactly who took it.
parsed.vision: Crustodian becomes the tiny robot that finally brings law to the shared fridge.
parsed.problem: A name written on a container is only a suggestion: the shared fridge is a lawless place with no witnesses.
parsed.target_users: flatshares where the container says DO NOT EAT, in marker, and it gets eaten anyway

parsed.name: Gnomecast
parsed.description: A solar-powered garden gnome that live-narrates squirrel activity in the voice of an increasingly invested sports commentator.
parsed.vision: Gnomecast becomes the garden ornament people leave the kitchen window open for.
parsed.problem: Garden pests get treated as a problem to be solved when they are, in fact, the best entertainment on the street.
parsed.target_users: gardeners who have named the squirrel that keeps defeating their bird-feeder engineering

parsed.name: Broth Runners
parsed.description: A social deduction board game that has players smuggling soup across a fantasy border while one of them is secretly the customs inspector.
parsed.vision: Broth Runners becomes the game night that ends in laughter, betrayal, and one strongly worded house rule.
parsed.problem: Every group has played the same three deduction games to death and now knows exactly how each other lies.
parsed.target_users: game groups who can recite each other's tells after six years of the same three deduction games

parsed.name: Petition
parsed.description: A paw-operated intercom that lets pets file formal complaints, which arrive as time-stamped voice notes on your phone.
parsed.vision: Petition becomes the official grievance procedure every household pet has been demanding for centuries.
parsed.problem: Pets currently communicate by knocking things off tables — an unstructured feedback channel with no audit trail.
parsed.target_users: cat owners who already answer out loud when the cat stares at a full bowl and screams

parsed.name: Sighence
parsed.description: A lapel pin that counts your sighs per hour and charts them against your calendar.
parsed.vision: Sighence becomes the wearable that turns a vaguely terrible week into a chart you can show someone.
parsed.problem: Wearables obsess over steps and sleep while ignoring the vital signs of office survival.
parsed.target_users: knowledge workers who suspect the recurring Thursday 2pm is why they feel like this, and want receipts

parsed.name: Kevinproof
parsed.description: An office coffee grinder with a fingerprint lock and a bean ledger that grinds only your beans, weighs every gram taken, and posts a weekly leaderboard of who took whose.
parsed.vision: Kevinproof becomes the appliance that settles the office bean wars with data instead of passive-aggressive sticky notes.
parsed.problem: The office kitchen runs on an honour system that collapses the moment someone brings in a good single-origin bag, and there is never any evidence — only suspicion and an empty jar.
parsed.target_users: coffee-obsessed office workers locked in a passive-aggressive hunt for the perfect brew and for whoever keeps taking their beans

parsed.name: Toastmood
parsed.description: A countertop toaster that asks how your morning is going and browns the bread to match, from "pale and hopeful" to "carbonised".
parsed.vision: Toastmood becomes the appliance that finally admits toast is an emotional decision.
parsed.problem: Toasters offer a numbered dial that means nothing, so every slice is a gamble placed before anyone is awake enough to gamble.
parsed.target_users: people who set the dial to 4, get charcoal, and start every day negotiating with an appliance

parsed.name: Sulk
parsed.description: A plush storm cloud that glows brighter and rumbles louder the longer it is left abandoned on the floor.
parsed.vision: Sulk becomes the toy that does the nagging so nobody in the house has to.
parsed.problem: Tidying up is a nightly argument because toys have no opinion about being left underfoot.
parsed.target_users: families who step over the same three abandoned toys nightly on the way to the tidy-up argument

parsed.name: Mimicorn
parsed.description: A plush axolotl with a hidden microphone that repeats the last thing it heard in a tiny, slightly wrong voice.
parsed.vision: Mimicorn becomes the toy that gets confiscated at bedtime and smuggled back by breakfast.
parsed.problem: Talking toys cycle through the same forty phrases until the batteries die, and children find the pattern in an afternoon.
parsed.target_users: parents of six-year-olds who have just discovered that repeating everything back is comedy

parsed.name: Afterclerk
parsed.description: A cozy management game that puts you behind the counter of a permit office for ghosts who are extremely particular about paperwork.
parsed.vision: Afterclerk becomes the comfort game that makes admin work feel like a warm bath.
parsed.problem: Management games simulate empires; nobody serves the player who just wants a tidy desk and a satisfied customer.
parsed.target_users: people who unwind by sorting other people's paperwork and would prefer the customers to be haunted

parsed.name: Krakenpark
parsed.description: A physics puzzle game that has you parallel-park increasingly enormous sea creatures into increasingly small harbours.
parsed.vision: Krakenpark becomes the game people sink sixty hours into and describe to friends as "you park a whale".
parsed.problem: The store is full of games about saving the world and nearly empty of games about doing a small, strange task perfectly.
parsed.target_users: players who bounced off world-saving epics and want to be quietly excellent at reversing a blue whale into a fishing berth

parsed.name: Truce
parsed.description: A thermostat with a voting panel that requires a quorum before anyone can change the temperature and keeps a log of who keeps trying.
parsed.vision: Truce becomes the end of the thermostat cold war, complete with an audit trail.
parsed.problem: A thermostat has one setting and many stakeholders, so the coldest-blooded person wins by stealth every single afternoon.
parsed.target_users: households where one person wears a fleece indoors and another opens windows in February

parsed.name: Fogoff
parsed.description: A desk-mounted fog machine and status lamp that releases a small dramatic fog cloud when your focus timer starts and glows green when you are interruptible.
parsed.vision: Fogoff becomes the availability signal readable from across the room, with theatre.
parsed.problem: Headphones are ambiguous, do-not-disturb statuses are invisible from three desks away, and saying "I am busy" out loud all day is exhausting.
parsed.target_users: open-plan developers whose deep work ends with a fourth cheerful "got a sec?" before lunch

parsed.name: Bailout
parsed.description: A calendar assistant that invents a plausible, escalating excuse and calls you out of any meeting that runs twenty minutes over.
parsed.vision: Bailout becomes the escape hatch every over-booked calendar quietly needs.
parsed.problem: Leaving a meeting early takes either courage or a believable emergency, and almost nobody has one on hand at 4pm.
parsed.target_users: people whose 3pm quick sync has run twenty minutes over every week since March
